subject: 'Need more? Take it!... Rs 1,299' - readers buried under a mountain of newspapers
alt: Kumar Alok's cartoon: on the left an elderly woman with grey-white hair, glasses and a green sari stands smiling; a pile of newspapers is tucked under one arm and she holds one out with the other. Her speech bubble reads 'NEED MORE? TAKE IT!... RS 1299!' On the right is a whirlwind of newspapers, sheets flying through the air, some carrying picture boxes. Three people are caught in the pile: a man in a white kurta with a moustache looks up anxiously over a paper in his hands; behind him a man with a black moustache holds a paper above his head in anger; and at the right a woman with long black hair in a pale yellow sari stands surrounded by papers, annoyed. At the bottom right, hands stick out from under the pile of paper. Alok's signature is at the lower left.
chutki: An elderly woman holds a pile of newspapers, holds one out with a smile and says, 'Need more? Take it!... Rs 1,299!' In front of her people are trapped in a storm of newspapers: sheets fly, one man looks up in worry, another is angry, a woman is buried, and hands poke out from under the paper.

The needle is that nobody asked for 'more'. A newspaper is supposed to bring news, but here the count is of pages and copies: the more the better, and for Rs 1,299 the reader gets a mountain of paper on his head. The one who sits down to read is drowning; the one who is selling is smiling.
